specPoints.text: explain why there is a change in the observed frequency and wavelength of a wave when its source is moving relative to an observer, and that this is known as the Doppler effect

primer.text: You already know that a wave carries a fixed frequency from its source and that speed depends on the medium. Put a moving source into that picture and the pattern bends: observers ahead and behind disagree about the pitch they hear. This lesson names that disagreement the Doppler effect and explains it with wavefronts.

lessons.title: The Doppler effect
sourceHeadings: A stationary source of sound waves
lessons.opening: A stationary siren pushes out wavefronts evenly in every direction, so everyone nearby hears the same pitch. Let the siren drive past and the picture skews: wavefronts pile up ahead of the motion and stretch out behind it. Observers therefore hear a higher pitch as it approaches and a lower pitch once it recedes, which is the Doppler effect.
keyPoints: The Doppler effect is the apparent change in observed wavelength and frequency from a moving source.
A stationary source emits wavefronts that spread out symmetrically.
Ahead of a moving source, wavefronts bunch so the wavelength appears shorter and the frequency higher.
Behind a moving source, wavefronts stretch so the wavelength appears longer and the frequency lower.
The speed of the emitted waves stays constant; only the observed wavelength and frequency shift.

low.restatement: When the source moves, each new wavefront starts from a spot slightly further along, so the rings crowd together in front and spread apart behind.
low.analogy: A walking person dropping a pebble every second: for a walker ahead of them the pebbles arrive closer together, for someone behind, further apart.
low.examPointer: The classic context is a siren passing you: say pitch falls as it passes, and tie it to wavelength stretching behind.

medium.restatement: Because wave speed is fixed by the medium, a shorter apparent wavelength must pair with a higher apparent frequency; the effect is a redistribution of the same wavefronts, not a change at the source.
medium.analogy: A stamper moving across paper while stamping regularly: prints crowd in the direction of travel and spread behind, though the stamping rhythm never changed.
medium.examPointer: Quote the conservation: speed constant, so wavelength decrease means frequency increase; that pairing is the mark scheme line.

check.stem: The Doppler effect is the apparent change in:

options.explanation: Wave speed stays fixed by the medium.

options.text: observed wavelength and frequency from a moving source
options.explanation: Both observed quantities shift when the source moves relative to the observer.
The effect concerns wavelength and frequency, not size of swing.
The source emits unchanged; the shift is observed.

check.stem: A stationary siren emits wavefronts that spread:

options.explanation: That pattern needs a moving source.
Sirens emit in all directions.
With no motion, every direction is equivalent.
The wavefronts spread as expanding rings.

check.stem: An observer stands in front of an approaching siren. Compared with the emitted wave, the observer receives:

options.text: a longer wavelength and a lower frequency
options.explanation: That is what an observer behind hears.
The whole point of the effect is the apparent shift.

options.text: a shorter wavelength and a lower frequency
options.explanation: The pairing violates the fixed wave speed.

options.text: a shorter wavelength and a higher frequency
options.explanation: Wavefronts bunch up ahead of the motion.

check.stem: After a police car passes and drives away, the observed pitch an observer hears:

options.text: drops, because the wavefronts stretch behind the car
options.explanation: Receding sources give longer apparent wavelengths and lower frequencies.

options.text: rises, because the car gains distance
options.explanation: Distance alone does not raise pitch; the stretching pattern lowers it.

options.text: stays the same as when it approached
options.explanation: Approach and recession give opposite shifts.
The sound continues, just at lower pitch.

check.stem: Light from a galaxy appears redder than emitted. This shows the galaxy is:

options.explanation: Approach would shift light bluer, not redder.
A stationary source shows no shift.
Redder light means longer apparent wavelength, the recession signature.

options.text: emitting at a lower frequency by nature
options.explanation: The effect is apparent, caused by motion, not a changed emitter.

check.stem: State what happens to the observed wavelength of a wave from a source moving towards you.
check.modelAnswer: The observed wavelength appears shorter, because the wavefronts bunch together ahead of the moving source.

check.stem: State the everyday example of the Doppler effect heard in traffic.
check.modelAnswer: A siren or engine drops from high pitch to low pitch as the vehicle passes and recedes.

check.stem: Explain why the wave speed does not change in the Doppler effect even though the observed frequency does.
check.modelAnswer: Wave speed is fixed by the properties of the medium, not by the source motion, so the only way the pattern can change is in its spacing and arrival rate, which is why wavelength and frequency shift together and oppositely.

check.stem: An ambulance drives past a pedestrian at constant speed with its siren on. Describe and explain how the pitch heard changes from before the ambulance reaches the pedestrian to after it has passed.
check.modelAnswer: Before it passes, the ambulance approaches so wavefronts bunch and the pitch sounds high; after it passes, the ambulance recedes so wavefronts stretch and the pitch drops, even though the siren emits at one constant frequency throughout.

glossary.definition: The apparent change in observed frequency and wavelength when a wave source moves relative to an observer.
Describing a change that depends on where the observer stands, not on any real change at the source.
A line joining points that vibrate in step, drawn spreading from a wave source.
